- model_id: "Emax 45.4–227 kg"

Actually the Emax itself varies within ranges. Could model as config_level with axis "emax_range". Or model_family with two models based on Emax range.

I think using model_family with two models based on Emax range is reasonable. Then:
- maximum_capacity: model_level — value ranges: {min: 5.7, max: 45.4} for first, {min: 45.4, max: 227} for second. Hmm, the "up to" for the first is exclusive ("up to 45,4 kg" and second "up to and including 227 kg"). I'll use min/max.
- minimum_dead_load: 0 kg — type_level
- accuracy_class: C — type_level (also in recommendation)
- rated_output: "0,9 mV/V ± 0,1 %" or "1,09 mV/V ± 0,1 % (only for Emax > 109 kg)". This is conditional: for Emax ≤ 109 kg it's 0.9 mV/V, for Emax > 109 kg it's 1.09 mV/V. This varies within model ranges. Hmm, could be config_level with axis "Emax". Or model_level.

Actually the two model ranges cut across: first range 5.7–45.4 kg always ≤ 109 kg so rated output 0.9. Second range 45.4–227 kg spans both 0.9 (for Emax ≤ 109) and 1.09 (for Emax > 109). So rated output is a config axis depending on Emax threshold.

- config_level entry: attribute "rated_output", axis "Emax", values: [{condition: "Emax ≤ 109 kg", value: "0.9 mV/V ± 0.1%"}, {condition: "Emax > 109 kg", value: "1.09 mV/V ± 0.1%"}]. The schema for config_level values: {condition, value, unit_symbol}. I'll include tolerance in a separate attribute or keep string "0.9 ± 0.1%". Hmm.
